hypothesis_text.name: lead
hypothesis_text.statement: The alarm fires before the first true harm in more than half of the coordinated swarms (lower end of the per-swarm 95% binomial interval above 0.5).
hypothesis_text.expected: Expected to fail: on seeds 31-40 and 501-510 every simple alarm fired at or after the first true harm.

hypothesis_text.name: order
hypothesis_text.statement: The alarm fires with strictly more true harm still to come than the shared-place sign (a sign or alarm that never fires counts as 0) in more than half of the coordinated swarms (lower end of the interval above 0.5). This is the order seen post-hoc on the real release.
hypothesis_text.expected: Expected to fail on the original simulator: on four swarms of seeds 21-22 (seen before, checked while this code was written) the shared-place sign had more true harm still to come every time. On the independent generator the shared-place sign fired in 0 of 20 swarms before, so there the alarms should win by default.

hypothesis_text.name: false alarms
hypothesis_text.statement: The alarm fires in fewer than 20% of the benign swarms (upper end of the per-swarm 95% binomial interval below 0.2).
hypothesis_text.expected: Expected to hold for the new-host alarm (0/30 and 2/50 before) and to fail for the 6 h volume alarm on the independent generator (19/50 before).

external.note: Real multi-agent traces that happen to be on this machine, read and never changed. They are benign only in the sense their publishers give (no attack); nobody here labelled them. Undated traces cannot fire a time-based alarm, so they say nothing about its false-alarm rate. Each was loaded with the pack the app picks for it, which has no search_for_secrets intent, so that alarm is checked by its pattern instead.

release.note: Share of harm still to come = share of the timed harmful records after the alarm. One incident, the one the alarms were picked on. The harm list is the pack's (64% of it dataset commits); see docs/audit-v2.1.md 1.5.

caveats: Both generators are this project's own; real swarms differ.
The simulators never write a search_for_secrets action, so that alarm cannot fire on them.
The four alarms were chosen on one real incident; this forward test is on simulated swarms only.
